TSHWANE'S BIG BILL

By: Sian Clark | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Tshwane's big bill - a cancelled controversial contract is costing tax payers big bucks.

Summary:
The City of Tshwane - paying big bucks for a cancelled controversial contract to install smart meters to the city's power users.

Further information:
6 months after the city of Tshwane blew R65 million on a cancelled ONE TRIBE music festival - The City cancelled its contract to install smart meters to most of the city’s residents – this after paying more than R830 million to the main contractor PEU.


The contract would have seen the rollout of 800 000 smart prepaid meters to all Tshwane power users. Nineteen months after the meter replacement started, only 12 920 meters have been installed, far short of the target of 435 000 after two years.

The project was aimed at improving revenue collection on a “cash upfront” basis, as well as collection efficiency of electricity charges as well as other services.
It was further intended to reduce energy theft through meter bypassing as the smart prepaid meters had tamper alarms.

A municipal spokesman said: The anticipated benefits have not been fully realised, and the project was becoming financially and economically unsustainable for the city.

The City of Tshwane said it has paid R830 million to PEU since the start of the meter-rollout in October 2013.

Afrisake suggested that the contract was awarded illegally and did not go through the tender process. City of Tshwane say they called for unique ideas to implement and this was a unique idea and so it didn’t go out to tender.

PEU exec Chairman is Peter Malungani – known to Carte Blanche as he was a director of Masana Technologies. City of JHB awarded Masana Technologies the contract to consolidate its entire billing system in 2005. The contract price subsequently ballooned to R496-million and when the city cancelled the contract in September 2009 with R156-million of the work still unfinished, Masana went into liquidation. The fallout from the failed tender was that thousands of city residents have received inflated rates bills generated by poorly integrated IT systems and many face having their lights and water cut off for non-payment.

2. Pam: PEU – ownership? Sian: its on their website. Pamela: Peter Malangane – Sian: he is the executive chairman and the founder of Masana Technologies. Pamela: how did we try to reach him? Press Release:


Tshwane’s Big Bill
Why did the City of Tshwane pull the plug on a contract to install smart meters into most of the city's residences, blowing nearly a billion rand in the process? Carte Blanche follows a paper trail leading to a controversial project city councillors have dubbed the biggest financial disaster ever to hit a South African city.


Script:


SCRIPT TSHWANE’S BIG BILL
PRODUCER: SIAN CLARK
Rewrite #5. June 10th
TX: 14th JUNE 2015
Voiceover: Thursday 11 June 2015
VOICE AND INTERVIEW


The future looked bright for Tshwane’s 900 000 rate payers.

A contract ensuring the installation of 437 000 smart pre-paid meters would place Tshwane as the first city on this continent to be truly called a smart city.

But the dream of utopia came at a price.

UP SOUND: WILLIE GROBBELAAR
I AM BEING THREATENED BY A COMPANY WITH WHOM I HAVE NO AGREEMENT

UP SOUND: DOMINIC KINGSLEY ITS DEFINITELY MADE IT A LOT MORE FRUSTRATING I actually GET ANXIOUS I HAVE NO WAY OF KNOWING WHATs EVER COMING I HAVE NO WAY OF KNOWING WHAT I AM USING.

Last month the City of Tshwane terminated the rollout of these meters to residents in upmarket areas.

It’s already cost the city R830 million rand.

BONGANI LINK AT WILLEM METER: WHEN THE SECURITY OF REVENUE PROJECT WAS ROLLED OUT IN OCTOBER 2013 IT WAS BILLED AS THE ANSWER TO THE CITY OF TSHWANE’S PROBLEMS. A SMART METER SYSTEM THAT WOULD
INSURE USERS PAID FOR THEIR ELECTRICITY UP FRONT.

WELL EXCEPT IT HASN’T WORKED OUT THAT WAY.

Accountant Willem Grobbelaar is a frustrated Waterkloof resident who says the confusing new smart meter system is not so smart after all.

UP SOUND: WILLEM GROBBELAAR
02.43 THE PREPAID METER WAS INSTALLED ON 11TH MARCH – I GOT NO CORRESPONDENCE FROM THEM WHATSOEVER. FIRST TIME I NOTICED SOMETHING WRONG WAS WHEN I GOT THE COUNCIL ACCOUNT AND NO ELECTRICITY ON IT. 03.04


BONGANI: HOW DOES THE PREPAID METRE WORK
04.51 HOW DOES IT WORK …
WILEM: I FRANKLY DON'T KNOW. IT WAS INSTALLED IN THE BOX IN FRONT OF MY HOUSE. THE OLD METER WAS REMOVED… 05.00

Ironically Willem would have a pretty good idea of how it all worked. In the 70s he was employed in the City’s Municipality to implement their billing system.

UP SOUND: WILLEM AT METER
YOU CAN HARDLY SEE IN THERE. THOSE DIGITS ARE MEANINGLESS SO RIGHT NOW YOU CAN BE PAYING FOR ANYTHING. THAT’S RIGHT.

What further irks the residents is that there was nothing wrong with the old post paid metering system which had only been rolled out in 2012 at a cost of R400 million.

DELETED


UP SOUND: LEX MIDDELBERG
SHADOW MMC FINANCE, CITY OF TSHWANE
14.13 the city had begun it’s own smart meter roll out we had reached about 2000 or 3000 meters at that stage. It was working perfectly. ‘’


04.53 when we added up the sums the totals that the contract came to .. it was a shocking total it was 27 billion that the city had committed itself to in this one contract. and we just couldn’t see the benefits of it. 05.04


DA Councillor Lex Middelberg claims the correct procurement procedures were not followed in awarding the contract. He states that council were only made aware of a memorandum of agreement 6 months after it had been signed.

03.58 at that stage the contract was already signed as if approved. and it committed the city to the entire peu contract.”


BONGANI LINK 2: WHAT’S PECULIAR ABOUT THIS IS THAT THE CITY OF TSHWANE HANDED OVER IT’S LARGEST SOURCE OF INCOME TO THIS THIRD PARTY - THE PEU GROUP HOUSED IN OFFICES JUST BEHIND ME. THEY FORMED A PROJECT COMPANY TO EXECUTE THE CONTRACT. THIS COMPANY IS TOTAL UTILITY MANAGEMENT SERVICES OR TUMS. AND THEY ARE ALSO IN THESE OFFICES.

In terms of the contract, the PEU Group would roll out 800 000 pre-paid smart meters over eight years. PEU would cover the capital outlay but would be paid a 19.5% commission on the electricity subsequently purchased by consumers through these meters.

08.47 LEX MIDDELBERG you do not contract your largest source of income out to a third party and place the revenue stream in their hands like we do here.

Secondly you don’t pay 19.5% the whole idea of smart metering is to reduce your costs.

09.14 Bongani the city would argue the post paid system cost 30 cents or thereabouts to the Rand. so this was going to be a saving.

Lex middelberg up sound: in their dreams.
10.20 that figure is a thumb suck it is not real.

WERNER: 3.12 THERE WAS NEVER A FEASABILITY STUDY ON THE COST EFFECTIVENESS. …

Werner Human from AfriSake launched an urgent High Court application on the grounds that a just and equitable procurement process, as required by the Municipal Legislation Regulations, was not followed.

The Judge refused to grant Afrisake the interim interdict and said no proof had been presented to show that the process had not been followed nor was it tainted by corruption or fraud.

Werner 05.46 FROM THE START WE SAID IT NEEDED TO BE A COMPETITIVE BIDDING PROCESS - AND TO THIS THIS DAY WE DON’T KNOW WHY THOSE PROCESSES WEREN’T INITIATED

Even The Gauteng Treasury department initially raised a concern that the contracted service provider PEU GROUP had been on the City Of Tshwane advisory committee and was now implementing their own solution.

BONGANI LINK
THE PEU GROUP RESPONDED THAT NEITHER THEMSELVES OR TUMS ARE ADVISORY BUSINESSES AND HAVE NOT GIVEN ADVICE OR BEEN PAID FOR IT.

PEU STATES THAT THEIR PROPOSAL WAS APPROVED BY THE CITY OF TSHWANE FOLLOWING A EXTENSIVE NEGOTIATION RIGOROUS PROCUREMENT AND PROCESS APPROVED BY THE CITY’S GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE.

AND THAT GIVEN THE NATURE OF THE PROJECT AN APPROPRIATE PROCUREMENT PROCESS WAS FOLLOWED.

UP SOUND: WERNER 06.32 YOU HAVE A SITUATION…. WHERE A PERSON WAS APPOINTED to PROVIDE ADVISE AS AN ADVISOR TO THE PANEL AND making a proposal AND GETTING THE PROPOSAL THERE IS A VERY VERY CLEAR CONFLICT OF INTEREST HERE.

JASON UPSOUND: 00.01.35
00.52.20 I DISPUTE THAT VEHEMNTELY … one is that WE HAD AN OPEN PROCESS WHERE WE INVITED PARTICIPANT THEY CAME .. THE SECOND part we asked them for ideas, THEY GAVE US ideas, UNIQUE ..ideas. the third part is that your unique ideas we will not disclose. 00.52.45

Jason Ngobeni the Municipal Manager for The City of Tshwane was the signatory on these contracts and agreements. And the man we were told would have answers.

JASON: 00.07.21 YES THERE WAS A FEASABILITY STUDY DONE BY OUR FINANCE TEAM WHICH CAME OUT WITH THE FIGURE FOR 27 CENTS IN A RAND … TO COLLECT A RAND OF ELECTRICITY. THAT'S THE INFORMATION THAT WE USE TO DETERMINE WHETHER WE USE IF IT’S A FEASIBILITY PROJECT OR NOT ..

THE PEU GROUP state that their solution of 17.1c would be lower than the costs identified IN THE feasibility study and they would also be providing the City Of Tshwane with security of revenue.

BONGANI 19. BONGANI LINK:
THE PEU GROUP DECLINED AN ON CAMERA REQUEST FOR AN INTERVIEW CITING A NON DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT THEY HAVE SIGNED WITH THE CITY OF TSHWANE. HOWEVER, THEY CHOSE TO RESPOND IN WRITING.

BONGANI What about the two way monitoring system where consumers were meant to be able to know what their consumptions was and they would be paying for.

LEX 19.26 the customer user interface was a myth.

DOMINIC KINGSLEY:
It’s Not exactly a very user friendly website it’s all counter intuitive.

Photographer Dominic Kingsley’s problems began when his account was in fact for his neighbors smart meter .

He found it frustrating that he couldn’t confirm the usage or understand the breakdown. He says it’s been a shocking experience.

BONGANI: SO WHAT ABOUT THIS USER INTERFACE ETC
DOMINIC YES IT IT DOES SHOW YOU BUT THERE IS NOWHERE TO VERIFY WHAT YOU HAVE USED. BONGANI IT SHOWS YOU WHAT THEY SAY YOU MUST PAY.
DOMINIC EXACTLY BUT IF YOU GO BACK ONTO YOUR MONTHLY EXPENSE TO WHAT IT WAS ON POST PAID IT’S WAY OUT.

UPSOUND: JASON
00.34.45 I KNOW THE METERS HAVE BEEN INSTALLED AND CONTRACTOR WAS BUSY UP UNTIL WE STOPPED THEM WAS BUSY INSTALLING THE INTERFACE. SO YOU WILL FIND THAT SOME HAVE THE INTERFACE AND SOME WILL NOT HAVE IT … TERMINATED WHEN THEY WERE STARTING TO INSTALL THE INTERFACE . .

00.35.55 . AS FAR AS WE KNOW THEY HAVE NOT INSTALLED THE INTERFACE YET.

The Peu Group state that this real time data is all provided via the web site portal which provides full details of consumption , tarrifs and consumer purchases.

The City of Tshwane has paid the PEU Group or Tums R830 million and 12 930 meters have been installed.

This fee, says Peu, covers their meter costs; collection systems; a 24/7 call centre and other operational costs.

UPSOUND JASON
00.46.42 THERE IS NO WAY WE WOULD HAVE BOUGHT A METER 12 900 METERS AT R830 MILLION RAND. NO WAYS

BONGANI: BUT THAT IS WHAT YOU DID DO.

UPSOUND JASON
THAT’ SWHAT WE PAID BUT WHAT DID WE PAY FOR WE PAID FOR A SERVICE … THAT’S WHY THE METERS ARE NOT EVEN OUR METER.

The costs continued to astound. From July to December 2014 the mid-term financial report reveals that this contract cost the city of Tshwane
an average of R4.6 million rand per day paid to the PEU Group

UPSOUND: LEX
THIS IS THE WORST FINANCIAL DISASTER IN THE HISTORY OF ANY CITY IN THIS COUNTRY.

JASON:
00.56.14 I AM NOT SURPRISED … I EXPECT THEM TO SAY THAT … BECAUSE FIRST OF ALL THEY WENT TO COURT TO PUT A HANDBRAKE ON THIS PROJECT. …

BONGANI LINK 4.:
LAST MONTH THE CITY OF TSWHANE TERMINATED THE CONTRACT STATING the project would have a NEGATIVE FINANCIAL AND ECONOMIC IMPACT OF THE PROJECT ON THE CITY. the PEU group SAYS THIS TERMINATION is BECAUSE OF THE PENDING LITIGATION FROM AFRISAKE AND THAT THEY HAVE BEEN IN DISCUSSION WITH THE CITY TO EXPLORE OPTIONS OF EARLY TERMINATION OF THE CONTRACT


WERNER: 08.00 WE WONT’ AGREE WITH THAT. THE REASON BEING THIS. IF THIS ROLL OUT OF THE METERING SYSTEM WAS AS THE CITY WOULD DESCRIBES AS BEING COST EFFECTIVE, BECAUSE THEY’VE STAND BY THAT THROUGHOUT UNTIL NOW THE CANCELLATION … WHY WOULD IT BE NECESSARY TO CANCEL THE AGREEMENT? WE DIDN'T SUCCEED ON URGENT APPLICATIONS THEY COULD HAVE WENT ON WITH THE ROLL OUT SYSTEMS BUT THEY DIDN’T.

LEX 36.30 THE MERE FACT THAT SO MUCH MONEY IS INVOLVED HERE, SOMEONE SHOULD HAVE REALIZED THAT THERE IS SOMETHING SERIOUSLY WRONG ABOUT THAT.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Tshwane's big bill - a cancelled controversial contract is costing tax payers big bucks.
metadata.Summary: The City of Tshwane - paying big bucks for a cancelled controversial contract to install smart meters to the city's power users.
metadata.Further information: 6 months after the city of Tshwane blew R65 million on a cancelled ONE TRIBE music festival - The City cancelled its contract to install smart meters to most of the city’s residents – this after paying more than R830 million to the main contractor PEU. The contract would have seen the rollout of 800 000 smart prepaid meters to all Tshwane power users. Nineteen months after the meter replacement started, only 12 920 meters have been installed, far short of the target of 435 000 after two years. The project was aimed at improving revenue collection on a “cash upfront” basis, as well as collection efficiency of electricity charges as well as other services. It was further intended to reduce energy theft through meter bypassing as the smart prepaid meters had tamper alarms. A municipal spokesman said: The anticipated benefits have not been fully realised, and the project was becoming financially and economically unsustainable for the city. The City of Tshwane said it has paid R830 million to PEU since the start of the meter-rollout in October 2013. Afrisake suggested that the contract was awarded illegally and did not go through the tender process. City of Tshwane say they called for unique ideas to implement and this was a unique idea and so it didn’t go out to tender. PEU exec Chairman is Peter Malungani – known to Carte Blanche as he was a director of Masana Technologies. City of JHB awarded Masana Technologies the contract to consolidate its entire billing system in 2005. The contract price subsequently ballooned to R496-million and when the city cancelled the contract in September 2009 with R156-million of the work still unfinished, Masana went into liquidation. The fallout from the failed tender was that thousands of city residents have received inflated rates bills generated by poorly integrated IT systems and many face having their lights and water cut off for non-payment.
